![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063674/assets/a7330541d6102141aec87f6733d09585553de672c5e55d2f84fe70196e4c6b5f.png)

The graph above shows $y={f}^{″}(x),$ where the function $f(x)$ is defined on $[-2,2].$ Find the intervals on which the function $f(x)$ is concave up.
worked_solution:
A function $f(x)$ is concave up over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={f}^{″}(x),$ we can see that ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ on the interval $(-1,1).$ Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is concave up on the interval  $(-1,1)$ only.
